info.title: Parikshaa
info.description: Assessment with a tamper-evident ledger and a micro-viva engine. Institution routes take a staff session token (from `POST /auth/login`) or an API key, and act within that account's organisation; candidate routes use a short-lived token scoped to one attempt, which is why they address it as `me`.

staffAuth.description: A staff session token (`pks_…`) or an API key (`pkk_…`).

get.description: Served from the same schemas the routes validate against, so it cannot drift from them.

post.description: Rejected with 422 and every problem at once if the exam is misconfigured.

post.summary: Set an attempt aside, with a recorded reason
post.description: A person's decision, so a signed-in user's and never an API key's. Nothing in the system reaches this on its own — no verdict, no confidence, no combination of them. The reason and who decided are written into the ledger and shown to the candidate.

reason.description: Recorded in the ledger and shown to the candidate. A short reason is rejected.
